extracted.intended_audience: municipal leaders, community-based organizations, and prospective applicants to the Kresge Foundation Environment Program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizations and municipal leaders seeking funding from the Kresge Foundation's Environment Program, including program priorities, focus areas, initiatives, strategies, and eligibility/apply instructions. Emphasizes equitable, community-driven climate solutions in urban contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program mission: link climate action and racial/economic justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Kresge’s Environment Program helps cities combat and adapt to climate change while advancing racial and economic justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program explicitly couples climate mitigation/adaptation work with racial and economic justice goals and expects proposals to reflect that integrated orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous mitigation and adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: We believe that cities should work on limiting climate change and preparing for its effects at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address both reducing greenhouse gas emissions and preparing communities for climate impacts rather than focusing solely on one approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centering impacted communities' voices
rubrics_metrics.description: We focus on making sure these community voices lead climate decisions — from city halls to state capitals to Washington, D.C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should demonstrate meaningful engagement and leadership by residents of the most-impacted neighborhoods, especially low-income communities and communities of color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to disproportionate harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate change hits some communities harder than others. The pollution that creates dangerous heat waves and severe storms causes the most harm in neighborhoods where people have lower incomes and in communities of color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should show awareness of inequitable exposure and design interventions that prioritize those most harmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment priority: Reduce greenhouse gas emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: We support efforts to: Reduce greenhouse gas emissions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded work should include measurable strategies to lower emissions in urban contexts (e.g., energy systems, transportation, buildings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment priority: Prepare for unavoidable climate effects
rubrics_metrics.description: We support efforts to: Prepare for the effects of climate change that cannot be avoided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to projects that increase resilience and adaptation capacity for communities facing imminent climate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment priority: Advance social cohesion and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: We support efforts to: Advance social cohesion and equity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should advance social cohesion and equity outcomes as a core objective, not an ancillary benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary audiences: municipal leaders and community-based partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work is driven by the needs of municipal leaders working on climate change and their community-based partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications from or in partnership with city governments and local community organizations are the central focus for this program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus area: Field Building
rubrics_metrics.description: Field Building — Supporting and strengthening leaders and organizations whose work is critical to addressing climate change while advancing racial and economic justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports capacity-building, leadership development, network-strengthening, and organizations that advance climate justice as a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus area: Transforming Urban Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforming Urban Systems — Accelerating equitable climate action in cities by transforming urban energy, health and water systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should aim for systems-level change in urban energy, health, and water infrastructure to produce equitable climate outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative: Climate Change, Health and Equity (CCHE)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCHE strengthens a unified movement for climate justice and health equity by advancing community-driven solutions and national movements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded CCHE work should link climate and health equity, emphasize community-driven approaches, and contribute to broader movement building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative: Climate Resilient and Equitable Water Systems (CREWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: CREWS transforms urban stormwater and wastewater systems to provide reliable and equitable services to all community residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects under CREWS should focus on equitable water-system transformation, improving reliability and access for underserved communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative: Equitable & Just Energy Transition (EJET)
rubrics_metrics.description: EJET — Facilitating an urban energy transition that eliminates carbon pollution, builds power for low-wealth communities and communities of color, and propels racial and economic equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals under EJET should demonstrate how energy transition activities reduce carbon and increase community power and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy: Public Sector Leadership Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Sector Leadership Support — Work to accelerate the efforts of public-sector leaders whose work is critical to advancing an equitable climate action agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is targeted to accelerate public-sector capacity and leadership to implement equitable climate policies and projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy: Climate Justice Movement Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate Justice Movement Support — Work to support leaders, organizations, and the network infrastructure to advance the climate justice movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding priorities include strengthening movement actors, coalitions, and the infrastructure that sustains climate justice organizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy: Community Development Climate Finance Ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Development Climate Finance Ecosystem — Work to strengthen community-focused co-developers, financing intermediaries, and technical assistance providers of climate-beneficial projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that build financing capacity, intermediaries, and TA models that enable community-driven climate investments are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding & eligibility constraint: unsolicited proposals not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Environment Program does not accept unsolicited proposals. When available, grant opportunities are listed on the Current Funding Opportunities page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should monitor the Current Funding Opportunities page for open solicitations and follow the specified application processes; general unsolicited applications will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application pathways & transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Apply (links and pages listing Environment Grants Made, Current Funding Opportunities, and program team).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the listed application pathways, review past grants for alignment, and connect with or learn about program staff roles to identify fit.
